reference: The harness GNU sed executable is the independent oracle for runnable cases. Expected status, stdout bytes, and in-place filesystem results are taken from its isolated run under LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC; the selected scripts use GNU/POSIX sed behavior described in the pinned sed documentation. No expected result is derived from the candidate.
coverage: BRE global substitutions, bracket classes, captures and replacement backreferences
ERE alternation with GNU case-insensitive and global substitution flags
quiet mode, line-address ranges, line-number output and explicit printing
multiline pattern space with N, embedded-newline substitution, and an unterminated final input record
labels and t branching while a line contains several substitutions
default cross-file line numbering versus -s separate-file numbering
-i backup creation, edited contents and backup contents
malformed regular-expression status and diagnostic presence
exclusions: A PTY case for canonical EOF followed by already queued bytes is deferred because the supplied runner provides no PTY fixture driver; pinned documentation records this as a known limitation.
This focused suite does not claim complete GNU sed command-line, locale-collation, non-Linux, or terminal equivalence.

cases.purpose: Check BRE bracket classes, two capture groups, backreference replacement, global replacement, and unchanged nonmatching input.
Check ERE alternation, GNU's I case-insensitive flag, and global substitution across upper- and lower-case matches.
Check -n, an inclusive numeric address range, and the = and p commands in a block.
Check N appending an unterminated final record to pattern space and substitution of the embedded newline.
Check label resolution and t branching after each successful substitution, then printing when no further match succeeds.
Check that a command from -e runs before a command read from -f: red becomes blue, then blue becomes green. Also checks relative script files in the fixture directory.
cases.script:
printf 's/blue/green/g\n' > changes.sed
printf 'red red\n' | sed -e 's/red/blue/g' -f changes.sed

cases.purpose: Check GNU's default stream-wide line numbering across operands and the per-file numbering enabled by -s.
cases.script:
printf 'a1
a2
' > first.txt
printf 'b1
b2
' > second.txt
sed -n '2p' first.txt second.txt
sed -s -n '2p' first.txt second.txt

cases.purpose: Check -i with a backup suffix. Stdout exposes both resulting files, while tree comparison also checks file bytes, modes, and the backup entry.
cases.script:
printf 'old old\nkeep\n' > doc.txt
sed -i.bak 's/old/new/g' doc.txt
sed -n '1,2p' doc.txt
sed -n '1,2p' doc.txt.bak

cases.purpose: Check -z record framing and substitution while preserving NUL separators in the byte output.
Check that an unmatched BRE opening group fails regex compilation with GNU's status and emits a diagnostic instead of silently passing input through.
Check the documented Bash-facing contract that sed is installed as a builtin with a help topic; this is metadata coverage, not sed operation coverage.
Compare GNU and candidate last-line handling when a canonical terminal EOF marker precedes already queued bytes.
cases.reason: Requires a bounded PTY fixture that can queue a canonical EOF marker followed by data while keeping the terminal open. The supplied runner launches fixtures with stdin connected to /dev/null and has no PTY driver. A future disposable Linux VM/PTY harness should retain the strict GNU comparison; pinned sed documentation records this ordering as a current limitation, but this case was not executed here.

cases.purpose: Hold-space append and transliteration preserve exact newlines.
Empty input is empty; missing file returns 2 while later operands are processed.
cases.script: : > empty; sed 's/a/b/' empty; printf 'a\n' > good; sed 's/a/b/' absent good
